$comment: The write guard's policy, read by scripts/agent-harness/write-guard/ and enforced, today, by the Claude Code hook generated from .agents/hooks.json into .claude/settings.json. A rule file is a path, relative to the root of any checkout that holds it, that a glob of ruleFiles matches: ** crosses folders, * stays inside one, letter case is ignored (the glob reader of scripts/manifest.mjs). A glob that starts ~/ is read against the path relative to the user's home folder instead. A .git file or folder below a checkout root is a rule path too, set in the engine, not here. Before a rule file is edited the guard asks the human, and it refuses a read-only agent (writes: false in .agents/agent-context.json), because the LAW 'A rule is not edited to fit the work' (AGENTS.md) lets a rule change only when the owner asks for that change. The list is F66's base list plus every file that could switch the guard off quietly, and .agents/harness.config.json, whose delivery.mergePolicy: low-risk grants an agent merge authority. No environment variable switches the guard off: Claude Code's own disableAllHooks: true, in the git-ignored .claude/settings.local.json, is the one way out. See docs/harness.md section 3f.
